newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine $2 bln bond attracted $6 bln in offers.
newsitem.headline: Argentine $2 bln bond attracted $6 bln in offers.

text.p: Argentine Treasury Secretary Pablo Guidotti, describing the $2 billion global bond issue as "very successful," said Tuesday it had been three times oversubscribed.

"It is a very successful placement which was only 80 basis points above Mexico's 20-year bond," Guidotti told reporters. "This demonstrates the good climate existing in the markets towards Argentina."
Guidotti said there were $6 billion in offers for the bond, which had a spread of 462.5 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
He said 75 percent of the $6 billion in offers came from the United States, 15 percent from Europe and 10 percent from Asia.
"We did better than expected in European and Asian markets," he said.
The treasury secretary added new investors took positions such as insurance companies and mutual funds "that are less likely to trade and more likely to keep them in the long run."
Argentina said previously it plans to issue $1 billion in additional bonds before the end of March. Guidotti said Tuesday that issue will probably be in marks.
He added that Argentina is studying offers to also issue 30-year dollar-denominated bonds.
The market was expecting a spread of 475 basis points on Tuesday's issue.
"The market shows greater confidence in Argentina than the credit rating agencies," Guidotti said. "The Argentine economy is solid and the credit ratings have not yet reflected that."
